newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close at third straight record.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close at third straight record.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed at a third straight record high led by market bellwether Electricidad de Caracas, traders said.

"Electricdad's tariff increase was very important and because of that the stock's still cheap," said Eduardo Soto, president of Delta brokerage, who cautioned that other shares looked increasingly expensive, however.
But he added: "While there's still demand for Electricidad, it's unlikely the rest of the market will fall."
The company, which regularly accounts for around a third of market trading volume, was last week awarded a 75 percent tariff increase to be phased in over the next six months.
The bolsa's .IBC index closed up 1.1 percent at 9,467.44 points as 34 shares rose, four fell and four closed flat.

Trade volume fell from recent highs to a more modest 89 million shares, worth 10 billion bolivars ($21 million), largely due to the United States' Independence Day market holiday, brokers said. Most of the day's turnover may have been by local investors, "but one still saw nonetheless a clear upward trend," Activalores trader Gonzalo Alonso said.

Among other widely traded stocks, telephone company CANTV rose 0.8 percent to 3,100.00 bolivars, even though Transport and Communications Minister Moises Orozco said the company's 1.98 percent third quarter tariff rise, due July 1, would be delayed.

"We've decided the tariff increase will not be approved while we're unsure as to the true structure of (the company's) costs," Orozco said. A second quarter 4.18 percent rate increase, due under the 1991 concession agreement, was similarly delayed and only finally granted on April 14.
